# BGP no_export and Well-Known Communities

## Thesis

**Well-known BGP communities** are a portable policy language. `no_export` (65535:65281) means "do not announce this route to eBGP peers"; `no_advertise` keeps it off all peers; `no_export_subconfed` stops it at confederation boundaries. Mis-applying them is a classic route-leak footgun.

## Mental model

```text
  route with community no_export
       │
       ├─ iBGP: still propagated inside the AS (usual)
       └─ eBGP: stripped from announcements to external peers
```

Vendor knobs differ: some require `send-community` on the neighbor before communities travel at all.

## Worked example

Conceptual FRR / policy sketch (lab with netlab/containerlab — not executed on this box; no sudo/lab installs):

```text
! tag a prefix so upstreams do not re-advertise it onward
ip prefix-list LOCAL-ONLY permit 192.0.2.0/24
route-map TAG-NO-EXPORT permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list LOCAL-ONLY
 set community no-export
!
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 203.0.113.1 remote-as 65002
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 route-map TAG-NO-EXPORT out
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 send-community
```

Verification on a lab router after the session is up:

```bash
show bgp ipv4 uni 192.0.2.0/24
# expect Community: no-export
# on the eBGP peer: prefix absent (or present only if they ignore well-known — treat as bug)
```

## Trap

**Assuming communities are sent by default.** Many implementations require an explicit `send-community [both]`. Also: `no_export` does **not** replace `NO_PEER` / RFC 7999 peer communities — pick the community that matches the business intent.

## Boring rule

Document each tagged prefix: who may see it, which community encodes that, and whether `send-community` is on. Test with an eBGP session in the lab before production.

## Try this

1. In netlab/containerlab, announce a prefix with and without `no_export` and watch the second-hop AS.
2. Compare `no_export` vs `no_advertise` on an iBGP mesh.
3. Read IANA well-known community registry values.

## Sources

- RFC 1997 (BGP Communities Attribute)
- RFC 3765 (`NOPEER`) / RFC 7999 (BLACKHOLE) as related well-knowns
